datasets.name: GraphVid-Bench
datasets.organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Sony Research India
datasets.description: A paper-described graph-conditioned image-to-video training and evaluation resource built around discrete object interactions, directed scene graphs, and fixed-duration motion clips.

access.notes: The paper describes the corpus and benchmark, but no official dataset files, annotations, or download procedure were available on 2026-07-26.

scale.notes: The reported category counts sum to 27,504 clips: 3,881 no-interaction, 10,982 single-interaction, and 12,641 multi-interaction examples.

license.media: Upstream and source-dependent
license.notes: The paper names WISA-80K, Something-Something v2, and MagicData as training sources and DAVIS 2017 plus MoveBench for evaluation; their original terms remain binding, and no GraphVid-Bench-specific license is published.

known_limitations: The corpus and its graph annotations are not publicly downloadable, so reported counts and construction steps cannot yet be independently audited.
Vision-language filtering intentionally excludes camera, ego-motion, background, and fluid-dynamics changes, narrowing the motion distribution.
Machine-generated entities and directed interaction edges can inherit errors and biases from the Qwen3-VL and embedding models used in construction.
Upstream dataset snapshots, per-source counts, duplicate handling, and media-rights composition are not disclosed.

processing.notes: The paper describes Qwen3-VL semantic filtering, motion-energy selection of 81-frame windows at 16 FPS, 512-by-288 dynamic letterboxing, and graph construction, but publishes no executable recipe.

datasets.name: OpenHumanVid-Talking
datasets.description: A speech-active talking-head subset derived from OpenHumanVid, with camera trajectories, active-speaker intervals, face and lip boxes, motion scores, captions, and clips packaged for audio-conditioned avatar training.

derived_from.contribution: Source talking-head videos from parts 001 through 040
derived_from.notes: The derivative selects motion-rich, speech-active, single-speaker intervals from OpenHumanVid and adds camera, face, lip, motion, and caption annotations.

access.notes: The public repository contains 17 Parquet shards, approximately 34 GB of embedded video data, and a companion NPZ annotation file.

scale.notes: The official card reports 32,176 clips and approximately 86 hours curated from OpenHumanVid parts 001 through 040.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-4.0 release terms layered on OpenHumanVid and original-source rights
license.notes: The derivative release is non-commercial; users must also satisfy OpenHumanVid and original-source conditions before redistributing or training on embedded media.

known_limitations: The set is derived only from OpenHumanVid parts 001 through 040 and may not represent the full source distribution.
Automated VAD, face, active-speaker, SLAM, camera-motion, and caption models can introduce false positives, exclusions, and geometric errors.
The public card does not provide detailed speaker, language, demographic, consent, or per-source rights distributions.
Non-commercial and layered upstream terms require review before media redistribution or production use.

processing.recipe: Select the highest-motion OpenHumanVid clips, require speech with Silero VAD, prefilter faces, retain TalkNet active-speaker islands of at least three seconds, estimate cameras with MonST3R, filter camera motion, and attach MediaPipe face and lip boxes plus Gemini captions.
processing.notes: Join Parquet videos and row metadata with the companion NPZ file when using the released DiffSynth-InContext-Control training path; preserve upstream part and source labels.

datasets.name: VITON-HD-edit
datasets.description: A public derivative of the 2,032-case VITON-HD test split that adds a synthesized same-person reference image and two garment-instance masks for image-editing try-on, segmentation, and spatial-control evaluation.

access.notes: The Hugging Face repository is directly downloadable and reports 6,096 image rows totaling about 377 MB.

scale.notes: Each VITON-HD test case gains three derived fields; the Hub viewer materializes those fields as 6,096 labeled image rows rather than 6,096 independent try-on cases.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 release layered on VITON-HD CC-BY-NC-4.0 source material
license.notes: Attribution and ShareAlike apply to the derived release; the upstream VITON-HD material is also restricted to non-commercial use and remains independently binding.

known_limitations: This is an evaluation derivative of the VITON-HD test split, not the private dataset used to train CtrlVTON.
It inherits VITON-HD's frontal-view women and upper-body clothing distribution, limiting demographic, pose, viewpoint, and garment-category coverage.
Reference-person images are synthesized and garment masks are generated by VIP-SAM, so generation and segmentation errors can affect all three supported evaluations.
The Hub viewer stores the three contributed image fields as separate rows, so row count must not be interpreted as independent benchmark cases.

processing.recipe: Apply the CtrlVTON data pipeline to all 2,032 VITON-HD test pairs, synthesize the same person wearing a different garment, then use VIP-SAM to extract the swapped-garment mask and the reference garment's target-person mask.
processing.notes: Preserve the original VITON-HD directory fields and join the three derived image fields by source case rather than treating viewer rows as independent samples.

datasets.name: GenSyn10
datasets.description: A 60,000-image synthetic benchmark aligned to ten CIFAR-10 classes, generated equally by FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage-3.0, and Qwen-Image-2512 for synthetic- image classification and cross-generator generalization research.

access.notes: The paper describes the full construction recipe, but no official dataset files or repository are currently linked.

scale.notes: Each generator contributes 20,000 images; the balanced split contains 50,000 training and 10,000 test images.

license.media: Generated-image terms remain dependent on the three source models
license.notes: The arXiv paper license does not establish a dataset license, and no dataset-specific usage or redistribution terms are published.

known_limitations: No official downloadable files, repository, or dataset-specific license were located during verification.
Images are downsampled from 512 by 512 pixels to 32 by 32 pixels, limiting conclusions about high-resolution generator artifacts.
The released recipe covers three generators and a template-based prompt grammar rather than open-domain production prompts.

processing.recipe: Generate balanced CIFAR-10-aligned classes at 512 by 512 pixels with three generators, then downsample with Lanczos resampling to 32 by 32 pixels.
processing.notes: Preserve the generator, class, split, prompt template, and generation configuration for each image if files are released.

datasets.name: Vera Layered Video Dataset
datasets.organization: Netflix and California Institute of Technology
datasets.description: A public layered video-editing corpus containing source, edit, alpha-matte, and composite videos built from VideoMatte240K plus human-curated Pexels and Mixkit footage for content-preserving object addition and background change.

derived_from.contribution: Accurately alpha-matted human foregrounds for synthetic composites
derived_from.notes: VideoMatte240K foregrounds and alpha mattes are paired with generated backgrounds and transformed into layered object-addition and background-change training tuples.

access.notes: Layered video files and metadata are hosted openly on Hugging Face; current repository storage is about 220 GB and may change with revisions.

scale.notes: The paper reports roughly 6K 81-frame training tuples and 486K frames. The hosted release exposes 11,996 49-frame train records, 6,005 81-frame train records, and 141 test records; these surfaces overlap and should not be interpreted as 18,142 independent source videos.

license.media: Apache-2.0 repository terms plus VideoMatte240K, Pexels Free License, and Mixkit Free License source conditions
license.notes: The dataset repository is Apache-2.0, while the source components retain their own licenses; verify stock-asset provenance and the exact source terms before production reuse.

known_limitations: Synthetic VideoMatte240K composites emphasize centered human subjects and static cameras.
Realistic stock-video subsets are filtered from Pexels and Mixkit and may not represent everyday, geographic, cultural, or long-form video distributions.
The corpus targets object addition and background replacement rather than the full space of video editing operations.
Hosted row and file counts reflect multiple frame-length variants and component layers, not unique source-video count.

processing.notes: Keep the four video layers joined by sample ID, preserve 49-frame versus 81-frame variants, task label, source family, resolution, and all alpha-matte precision.

datasets.name: MV-Fashion
datasets.organization: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and collaborators
datasets.description: A synchronized multi-view fashion capture dataset pairing clothed human performances with flat garment imagery, material and sizing metadata, segmentation, SMPL-X bodies, and reconstructed geometry.

access.notes: Access requires a Hugging Face account, manual approval, and acceptance of the dataset agreement for non-commercial research use.

scale.notes: The current release reports 52,020,529 frames, 2,357 sequences, 81 subjects, and about 11.5 TB; this is smaller than the paper headline of 72.5M frames and 3,273 sequences after privacy exclusions and quality removals.

license.media: MV-Fashion Dataset Agreement
license.notes: Access is limited to approved non-commercial research; the agreement and GDPR-sensitive human-subject restrictions prohibit treating the release as an unrestricted open corpus.

known_limitations: The current 52.0M-frame release differs materially from the paper's 72.5M-frame headline after privacy and quality exclusions.
Minimally clothed captures are excluded for privacy and GDPR reasons, and some annotations remain in progress.
Up to three cameras can be missing for a sequence, while removed bad frames and sequences make capture coverage non-uniform.
Approved research-only access prevents direct commercial deployment and unrestricted redistribution.

processing.recipe: Synchronize 68 cameras, calibrate RGB and depth views, remove privacy-sensitive and quality-failed captures, and align segmentation, SMPL-X, point clouds, garment catalog imagery, sizing, and material measurements.
processing.notes: Use the current manifest as the authoritative release scale, preserve per-camera missingness, and do not substitute the larger paper headline for downloadable counts.

datasets.name: MAVEN Multicultural Multiagent Videos
datasets.organization: Sichuan University and University of Washington
datasets.description: A compact benchmark of original and agent-refined prompts paired with generated videos for measuring mono-cultural and cross-cultural fidelity in text-to-video systems across Chinese, American, and Romanian settings.

access.notes: The complete 676 MB dataset is directly hosted as five-second MP4 videos and structured prompt metadata.

scale.notes: There are 243 prompt scenarios rendered through four pipelines, producing 972 five-second videos.

license.notes: The official dataset card releases the dataset under CC0 1.0.

known_limitations: Coverage is limited to three cultures and three action categories and cannot represent within-culture diversity.
Four outputs per scenario share prompts and generation pipelines, so rows are not statistically independent.
Synthetic outputs inherit biases and artifacts from the evaluated video generator and prompt-refinement agents.

processing.notes: Group evaluations by the 243 underlying scenarios and report mono-cultural and cross-cultural results separately.

datasets.name: GPIC
datasets.description: A centrally hosted, permissively licensed image corpus for visual generation, with 100M training images, held-out validation and test splits, multiple caption granularities, safety filtering, deduplication, and attribution.

access.notes: The repository is public but users must sign in, accept the conditions, and share contact information before accessing files.

scale.notes: The release contains 100M train, 200K validation, and 1M test examples, totaling about 28 trillion pixels.

license.media: Per-image permissive licenses with attribution records
license.notes: The maintainers state every image is licensed for research and commercial use; consumers must still preserve the per-item license and attribution metadata.

known_limitations: Model-generated captions can hallucinate or omit details and are primarily English.
Permissive licensing does not eliminate privacy, publicity, sensitive-content, or takedown obligations.
Safety and deduplication filters can introduce systematic coverage and representation gaps.

processing.notes: Stream the tar shards, retain the JSON record beside every image, pin a commit revision, and propagate removals across local mirrors.

datasets.name: ERIA-1K
datasets.description: A held-out, human-annotated image-aesthetics benchmark designed around a deployment-oriented mixture of photography, illustration, graphic design, mixed web imagery, film photography, and product imagery.

access.notes: The report says ERIA-1K is open-source, but no downloadable benchmark files are linked in the official resources.

scale.notes: The benchmark contains 1,000 images across six disclosed content categories.

license.media: Source-dependent and undisclosed
license.notes: The Apache-2.0 model license does not establish terms for the benchmark metadata or underlying images.

known_limitations: No official downloadable data files or dataset-specific license were located during verification.
The report gives category proportions but not the source-level provenance or rights composition of the images.
Professional calibration improves annotation consistency but does not make aesthetic judgments universal.

processing.notes: Preserve all six content categories and the Swiss-tournament-derived aesthetic tiers from 1 to 10.

datasets.name: RoVid-X
datasets.description: A four-million-clip robotic video corpus assembled from Internet and open embodied sources, with RGB, depth, optical flow, task descriptions, and physical-property annotations for embodied video generation.

access.notes: The official release is hosted as large WebDataset tar shards on Hugging Face and is directly downloadable without a gate.

scale.notes: The paper and release describe about four million annotated clips spanning thousands of robot tasks.

license.media: CC-BY-4.0 repository declaration plus source-specific rights
license.notes: The hosted card declares CC BY 4.0, but Internet videos and more than twenty upstream embodied datasets retain source-specific terms and provenance obligations.

known_limitations: Internet and multi-dataset aggregation can produce uneven rights, embodiment, task, camera, and geographic coverage.
Automatically derived depth, flow, captions, and physical properties require downstream validation.
The Hugging Face viewer exposes WebDataset shards rather than a simple row-wise schema.

processing.recipe: Collect robotic videos, filter quality, segment tasks, caption actions, and annotate physical properties, then package clips as WebDataset shards.
processing.notes: Preserve upstream-source, task, embodiment, RGB/depth/flow alignment, annotation version, and tar-shard provenance during extraction.

datasets.name: RBench
datasets.description: A 650-case robotics video-generation benchmark spanning five task families and four robot embodiments, with reproducible structure, physics, action, and visual-quality metrics.

access.notes: The validation images, prompts, metadata, and evaluator checkpoints total about 22 GB and are downloadable from the official Hugging Face repository.

scale.notes: Includes 250 task-oriented image-text cases and 400 embodiment-oriented cases.

license.media: CC-BY-4.0 repository declaration
license.notes: The official dataset card declares CC BY 4.0; retain attribution and review the evaluator checkpoints and any third-party dependencies separately.

known_limitations: Six hundred fifty cases cannot represent every robot, task, camera, environment, or failure mode.
Automated metrics depend on multiple external perception checkpoints and optional GPT-based evaluation.
The reported 0.96 human correlation is study-specific and may not transfer to new model or task distributions.

processing.recipe: Generate videos from each reference image and prompt, then run task- and embodiment-oriented scripts combining VLM judgments with low-level structure, motion, and quality operators.
processing.notes: Pin prompts, evaluator checkpoints, model outputs, metric versions, and API-backed judge settings for reproducible comparisons.

datasets.name: Lens-RL-8K
datasets.description: A taxonomy-driven prompt and rubric collection used to reinforce Lens after pretraining across diverse text-to-image scenarios, including people, objects, scenes, text rendering, and graphic design.

access.notes: The technical report describes the collection, but no official dataset download is currently linked.

scale.notes: The release identifies the prompt set as 8K rather than publishing an exact row count.

license.media: Not applicable; the described records are text prompts and rubrics
license.notes: No dataset-specific license or redistribution terms are published with the technical report.

known_limitations: The prompt set and complete rubrics are not publicly downloadable for independent inspection.
GPT-4.1 generated both prompts and prompt-specific rubrics, so model biases can propagate into RL coverage and rewards.
The 8K name does not establish an exact machine-verifiable row count.

processing.notes: Preserve taxonomy fields, prompts, up to ten prompt-specific rubrics, and the appended global rubric.

datasets.name: Lens-800M
datasets.description: The 800-million-pair training corpus named in the Microsoft Lens report, featuring long GPT-4.1-generated captions averaging about 109 words.

access.notes: The paper names and characterizes the corpus but does not publish a dataset download.

scale.notes: Scale is reported by the Lens authors.

license.media: Not disclosed
license.notes: The training corpus is described in the paper but its sources and terms are not disclosed.

known_limitations: Source composition, filtering thresholds, rights, and release plan are undisclosed.
GPT-4.1-generated captions can propagate model-specific biases or hallucinations.

processing.notes: Preserve caption-model version and original text if reproducing this strategy.

datasets.name: FIT-VTO-100K
datasets.organization: University of Washington and Google Research
datasets.description: The official 105,000-sample preview of the FIT fit-aware virtual try-on dataset, pairing lay-flat garments, neutral person images, try-on targets, and precise body and garment measurements.

access.notes: The repository exposes 100,000 training and 5,000 evaluation rows in Parquet, totaling about 212 GB.

scale.notes: Every row contains three aligned 768 by 1024 images; this preview is smaller than the full 1,069,824-sample FIT collection described on the project page.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 per the official dataset card
license.notes: Attribution is required; commercial use and distribution of derivatives are prohibited by the published dataset license.

known_limitations: The released 105K preview is a subset of the more than one-million-sample FIT collection described by the paper and project page.
Synthetic generation and re-texturing can leave a domain gap relative to real people, garments, lighting, and fabric behavior.
CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 prevents commercial use and derivative redistribution, which materially limits production training workflows.

processing.recipe: Generate parametric 3D garments, drape them over measured body shapes with physics simulation, re-texture renders into photorealistic paired images while preserving geometry, QA-filter lay-flat garments with Gemini 2.5 Flash, and regenerate failed garments with a try-off model.
processing.notes: Preserve all three aligned images plus body and garment measurements; images are resized or center-cropped and padded to 768 by 1024.

datasets.name: TripVVT-10K
datasets.organization: Nanjing University, JIUTIAN Research (CMCC), Jilin University, and ByteDance
datasets.description: An in-the-wild video virtual try-on corpus of synchronized input video, garment reference, and real target video triplets, with masks, pose, line maps, captions, and a 100-case held-out benchmark.

access.notes: The public repository requires users to sign in, accept the access conditions, and share contact information before downloading 18 tar shards of about 72.6 GiB.

scale.notes: The official split contains 9,931 training and 100 held-out benchmark triplets at 720 by 1280; construction begins from roughly 20,000 crawled source videos.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-4.0 claimed by the dataset card; underlying crawled-web provenance is not enumerated
license.notes: The published license prohibits commercial use, while the absence of per-video source URLs and upstream rights requires a separate review before redistributing media snapshots.

known_limitations: Source URLs, consent status, geographic distribution, and upstream media rights for the roughly 20K crawled human videos are not disclosed.
Input videos and garment references are synthesized, so residual identity shifts, temporal flicker, reconstruction errors, and generator biases can remain after filtering.
Access is manually gated and non-commercial, which limits unattended reproduction and production use.
The 100-case benchmark is small relative to the training split and may not capture all body types, motions, environments, or multi-person failure modes.

processing.recipe: Normalize and filter web videos, sample 121-frame clips, build temporal human masks, synthesize a garment-swapped first frame and guided-inpainting video, reconstruct a product-style garment image, filter with Gemini for fidelity and artifacts, manually review, then derive pose, line-map, and video-caption conditions.
processing.notes: Use the JSON or JSONL manifests to join MP4 videos and PNG conditions; preserve the 9,931/100 split and the reverse-training distinction between synthesized inputs and real target videos.

datasets.name: AVGen-Bench
datasets.description: A holistic benchmark for native and pipeline-based text-to-audio-video generation with 235 prompts across 11 content categories, 3,009 generated samples, multidimensional automatic metrics, and an official leaderboard.

access.notes: Prompt metadata and about 20.1 GB of generated benchmark videos are hosted on Hugging Face without a gate.

scale.notes: The official release contains outputs from 13 model or pipeline configurations for 235 prompts spanning 11 categories.

license.media: Generated model outputs subject to repository terms and each generator provider's output terms
license.notes: The Hugging Face repository is marked MIT, but generated output rights and embedded people, brands, music, speech, or text may require separate review.

known_limitations: The leaderboard mixes native joint generators and multi-model pipelines, so scores do not isolate every component model.
A 235-prompt suite cannot cover the full distribution of audiovisual storytelling, languages, cultures, safety, or long-form temporal structure.
Provider versions and inference settings can change after the fixed generated-output snapshot.

processing.notes: Preserve prompt category, exact generator or pipeline label, version, inference setting, output file, and metric version when reproducing comparisons.

datasets.name: Fine-T2I
datasets.description: A high-resolution text-to-image fine-tuning corpus that combines synthetic generations with curated professional photography, dual prompts, explicit task and style coverage, and aggressive alignment and quality filtering.

access.notes: WebDataset archives can be streamed from Hugging Face; the repository is large and has changed while the release was being completed.

scale.notes: The current card lists 6,145,693 synthetic samples plus 168,424 curated real images, totaling 6,314,117 pairs and about 2 TB.

license.media: Dataset release terms layered over synthetic outputs and licensed professional-photo sources
license.notes: The dataset card labels the repository Apache-2.0, but users should separately review the source platforms and generator-output terms for the underlying images.

known_limitations: Synthetic samples dominate the mixture and can reproduce the biases and artifacts of the source generators and prompt designer.
Quality filters reject more than 95 percent of candidates and may narrow visual, cultural, and aesthetic diversity.
The curated real-image subset inherits source-platform terms and photographer representation biases.

processing.notes: Pin the repository revision, stream shards, retain prompt variants and source type, and audit synthetic versus real mixture weights per training run.

datasets.name: Audiovisual Translation Dubbing Dataset
datasets.description: A released 288-record paired video collection for training synchronized audiovisual dubbing adapters, with source references, dubbed targets, multilingual structured captions, and optional facial masks.

access.notes: The public repository is approximately 537 MB and exposes one 288-row training split.

scale.notes: Each logical record pairs one reference video with one target dubbed video; optional face masks are additional assets.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-4.0 per the official dataset card
license.notes: Attribution and non-commercial restrictions apply; downstream users must also review the LTX-2 model terms used to generate and train on the media.

known_limitations: The 288-record scale is small relative to the diversity of speakers, languages, accents, poses, and production conditions in real localization workloads.
Face segmentation masks are optional, so mask coverage is not uniform across all records.
The public card does not enumerate per-language counts or the complete prompt and rejection distribution.

processing.recipe: Generate multilingual clips with language switches, use counterfactual face-and-audio inpainting to form same-speaker pairs, and compute latent-aware face masks for localized training losses.
processing.notes: Preserve the target-reference pairing, structured caption, language, dialogue, and optional mask path for every record.

datasets.name: VGGSound-Omni
datasets.organization: Tsinghua University, Monash University, and Shengshu AI
datasets.description: A unified audio-generation benchmark derived from the VGGSound test set with human-verified dense captions for more than 14,000 videos and a dedicated 1,613-item off-screen track spanning natural events and synthetic music.

derived_from.contribution: Primary benchmark videos from the VGGSound test split
derived_from.notes: The main VGGSound-Omni track reuses VGGSound test media with new dense captions, modality labels, human verification, and a separate off-screen extension.

access.notes: The benchmark is distributed with SoundAtlas after acceptance of the repository access terms.

scale.notes: The primary track covers 14,000+ VGGSound test videos; the off-screen track contains 1,613 items.

license.media: Source-dependent VGGSound, YouTube, and MusicCaps terms
license.notes: The benchmark repository is CC-BY-NC-4.0, while the underlying videos and mixed music retain source-platform and source-dataset conditions.

known_limitations: The benchmark is constructed by the Omni2Sound authors and can share their captioning-style biases.
Human review is targeted through an AI-assisted mismatch audit rather than described as uniform double annotation.
Part of the off-screen track is synthetically mixed and may not match natural background-music distributions.

processing.notes: Preserve primary versus off-screen track, natural versus synthetic origin, modality labels, and source media ID.

datasets.name: SoundAtlas
datasets.organization: Tsinghua University, Monash University, and Shengshu AI
datasets.description: A roughly 470-thousand-pair audio-caption corpus derived from AudioSet and VGGSound with temporally grounded descriptions of audible and visual context.

derived_from.contribution: Source audiovisual clips and event metadata
derived_from.notes: AudioSet is one of the two named upstream collections routed through SoundAtlas captioning and multimodal-consistency filtering.

derived_from.contribution: Source audiovisual clips and class metadata
derived_from.notes: VGGSound is one of the two named upstream collections routed through SoundAtlas captioning and multimodal-consistency filtering.

access.notes: Access requires accepting the repository terms and sharing contact information.

scale.notes: The project and paper consistently describe SoundAtlas as about 470K pairs.

license.media: Source-dependent AudioSet and VGGSound media terms
license.notes: The Hugging Face repository applies CC-BY-NC-4.0 to the release, while the underlying media remains subject to its original source and platform terms.

known_limitations: Source media availability and rights can change independently of the released annotations.
Model-generated captions can retain hallucinations despite multimodal consistency filtering.
The two upstream collections have different collection processes and label distributions.

processing.notes: Retain source identifiers, captioning-agent versions, alignment scores, and media-fetch status.

datasets.name: VideoCoF-50K
datasets.organization: University of Technology Sydney and Zhejiang University
datasets.description: The public training corpus for VideoCoF, pairing source videos, edit-region reasoning videos, edited targets, and natural-language instructions across object addition, removal, swap, and local style transfer.

derived_from.contribution: Filtered source videos for the four released local-edit task archives
derived_from.notes: VideoCoF-50K selects Señorita source clips, creates new synthetic edits and edit-region reasoning videos, and applies DOVER and VIE filtering rather than copying Señorita pairs unchanged.

access.notes: Hugging Face hosts JSON metadata and four task archives containing 49,177 rows and approximately 85.6 GB of released files.

scale.notes: The hosted release contains 49,177 rows; the paper reports the curated training mixture as 50,000 pairs split 10K addition, 15K removal, 15K swap, and 10K local style.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-4.0 release terms plus upstream source and generator dependencies
license.notes: The official dataset card is non-commercial; downstream users should also review the source-video and synthetic-teacher terms before redistributing media or derivatives.

known_limitations: The released 49,177 rows are slightly fewer than the paper's rounded 50K task mixture, and the per-task release delta is not explained.
Synthetic edits can inherit artifacts, safety issues, or biases from MiniMax-Remover, VACE-14B, GPT-4o, and Grounding DINO.
The four local editing tasks do not cover global edits, identity-driven edits, audio edits, or the full professional editing distribution.
Source-video provenance and rights are not enumerated per sample in the public card.

processing.recipe: Filter Señorita source clips; synthesize addition and removal pairs with MiniMax-Remover; generate swap and local-style pairs with VACE-14B, GPT-4o prompts, and Grounding DINO masks; create soft grayscale reasoning frames; then filter with DOVER and VIE scores.
processing.notes: Keep original, reasoning, and edited videos joined to the instruction and task type; pin the Hugging Face revision and retain the task archive manifest.

datasets.name: TalkVerse
datasets.description: The released metadata and annotation layer for TalkVerse's large-scale, human-centric audio-video training corpus, curated from OpenHumanVid and Panda-70M for audio-driven talking-video generation.

derived_from.notes: The public TalkVerse metadata exposes an OpenHumanVid partition of approximately 796K rows after TalkVerse-specific filtering and annotation.

derived_from.contribution: General human-related source videos and metadata
derived_from.notes: The public TalkVerse metadata exposes a Panda-70M partition of approximately 1.34M rows after TalkVerse-specific filtering and annotation.

access.notes: Access is automatically gated after accepting the conditions. The repository exposes metadata, captions, transcripts, poses, and source references rather than the underlying source videos; media must be obtained through the upstream datasets or original sources.

scale.notes: The public repository exposes approximately 796K OpenHumanVid rows and 1.34M Panda-70M rows; the paper instead reports 2.3M retained clips and 6.3K hours from a 30M-clip, 60K-hour source pool.

license.media: Not redistributed; OpenHumanVid, Panda-70M, and original-source terms remain binding
license.notes: The repository license applies to its metadata release, while every retrieved media item requires separate review against upstream access rules, licenses, and original-source rights.

known_limitations: The public release contains metadata rather than source media, so it is not a self-contained training corpus.
The approximately 2.14M public rows do not exactly match the paper's 2.3M-clip training count.
Item-level source rights, consent status, demographic composition, and geographic distribution are not normalized in the public card.
Automated person, subtitle, sync, language, caption, and pose models can introduce filtering and annotation bias.

processing.recipe: Normalize to H.264 at 25 fps, remove borders, split 5-to-50-second shots, filter visual quality, motion, people, subtitles, and audio-video synchronization, then add language, structured visual, audio-style, ASR, pose, and deduplication metadata.
processing.notes: Preserve upstream dataset and source identifiers when resolving media; keep the OpenHumanVid and Panda-70M partitions separate so licensing, availability, and scale remain auditable.

datasets.name: HuMoSet
datasets.organization: Tsinghua University and ByteDance Intelligent Creation Team
datasets.description: A human-centric multimodal video corpus pairing each target video with a same-identity but visually distinct reference image, a Qwen2.5-VL dense caption, and strictly processed synchronized audio for controllable generation.

derived_from.contribution: A documented source of public human-centric videos and reference imagery
derived_from.notes: The official card names OpenHumanVid as one example among multiple open-source source datasets; it does not disclose the exact contribution or full source mixture.

access.notes: ModelScope provides direct CLI and Git LFS download instructions for target videos, reference images, and video_caption.parquet; its API reports approximately 708 GB of repository storage.

scale.notes: The official release reports about 670,000 video samples, each with a distinct same-identity reference image and a dense video caption.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-ND release label layered on the licenses and rights of source datasets
license.notes: ModelScope exposes the label CC-BY-NC-ND without a version; users must inspect the repository LICENSE and every upstream dataset's terms before training, adapting, or redistributing the media.

known_limitations: The full source-dataset list, source proportions, deduplication method, and per-sample provenance are not published on the card.
Qwen2.5-VL captions and automated audio-visual synchronization filters can contain hallucinations, exclusions, or alignment errors.
Speaker language, demographic, consent, safety, and identity distributions are not documented.
The license version is not specified and upstream source rights remain layered, so commercial use and derivative redistribution require review.

processing.recipe: Curate videos and distinct same-identity reference images from public datasets, generate dense descriptions with Qwen2.5-VL, enhance and filter speech segments, and retain samples that pass audio-visual synchronization processing.
processing.notes: Download with the ModelScope CLI or Git LFS, join video and reference_image files through video_caption.parquet, and preserve source and license metadata when available.

datasets.name: OpenVE-Bench
datasets.description: A 431-pair benchmark for spatially and non-spatially aligned instruction-led video editing, covering the same eight edit categories as OpenVE-3M and using three metrics designed to track human judgments.

derived_from.contribution: Editing taxonomy, source and edited video pairs, and instruction format
derived_from.notes: The OpenVE project presents the benchmark as the held-out evaluation companion constructed with the OpenVE-3M pipeline and categories.

access.notes: The 431-row video benchmark is directly hosted on Hugging Face.

scale.notes: The project reports 431 video-edit pairs across eight fine-grained categories, averaging more than 50 clips per category.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-4.0 release terms plus source-dependent rights
license.notes: The Hugging Face card labels the benchmark CC-BY-NC-4.0; users should retain source provenance and review any component-media constraints.

known_limitations: A 431-pair benchmark cannot exhaustively cover instructions, subjects, motion, or professional editing styles.
Benchmark construction and metric design share the OpenVE taxonomy and may favor systems trained on similar edit distributions.

processing.notes: Keep task categories balanced in reporting and separate spatially aligned from non-spatially aligned scores.

datasets.name: OpenVE-3M
datasets.description: A large synthetic instruction-guided video-editing corpus spanning six spatially aligned and two non-spatially aligned edit categories, with source videos, edited videos, instructions, and rigorous generation-time filtering.

access.notes: Video archives and per-category CSV triplets are hosted on Hugging Face in a multi-terabyte release.

scale.notes: The project reports more than 3M editing triplets at 720p and 65 to 129 frames; the Hugging Face viewer estimates about 4.52M individual video rows because records include component media.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-4.0 release terms plus source and generator dependencies
license.notes: The official card marks the dataset non-commercial; source-video and synthetic-generator terms must also be reviewed for derived releases.

known_limitations: Synthetic edited targets can contain artifacts or biases inherited from the teacher pipeline.
The eight edit categories do not cover the full distribution of professional editing, localization, identity, or audio workflows.
Headline triplet counts and hosted row estimates use different units and should not be combined.

processing.notes: Keep original and edited videos paired with instruction and category, verify archive joins, and record teacher and filter versions when available.

datasets.name: Phantom-Data (Koala-36M release)
datasets.description: A cross-pair subject-to-video training release built on Koala-36M metadata, linking target clips and captions to same-identity or same-category reference frames drawn from different visual contexts to reduce copy-paste behavior.

derived_from.contribution: Source clip URLs, timestamps, captions, and clip-quality metadata
derived_from.notes: Phantom-Data adds cross-context subject detections, bounding boxes, reference-frame matches, and identity-verification results to Koala-36M clip metadata.

access.notes: The open Hugging Face repository hosts two Parquet metadata files totaling about 1.15 GB; source clips must be resolved separately from YouTube URLs and timestamps, and reference images are extracted from referenced frames.

scale.notes: The paper reports approximately one million identity-consistent pairs retrieved from more than 53 million videos and three billion candidate images.

license.media: Source-dependent Koala-36M and YouTube terms and uploader rights
license.notes: Hugging Face labels the metadata Apache-2.0, while the official repository restricts the dataset to non-commercial research; neither label grants rights to source videos or uploader content.

known_limitations: The release contains metadata and frame references rather than redistributable source videos or ready-to-train image files.
Source URLs can disappear or become restricted, and availability depends on the upstream Koala-36M and YouTube records.
Automated subject detection, retrieval, and prior-guided identity verification can introduce false matches and category or demographic bias.
The repository's non-commercial disclaimer is stricter than the Apache metadata tag and requires legal review before use or redistribution.

processing.recipe: Detect instruction-aligned subjects, retrieve cross-context candidates from large video and image pools, verify identity consistency with model priors, and publish target-to-reference mappings over Koala-36M metadata.
processing.notes: Download both Parquet files, resolve clips only after rights review, extract the referenced frame and bounding box, and preserve the Koala-36M source identifiers.

datasets.name: SpatialVID
datasets.organization: Nanjing University and Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
datasets.description: A large spatially annotated video corpus derived from 33,443 manually screened YouTube videos, providing 2.7 million 720p clips with camera poses, depth, dynamic masks, structured captions, and serialized motion instructions for controllable generation and geometric learning.

access.notes: Access is automatically gated behind a Hugging Face form and acceptance of the non-commercial share-alike license; official download scripts cover video and annotation archives.

scale.notes: The paper reports 2.7M clips and 7,089 hours after filtering 21,789 hours of source video; SpatialVID-HQ is a balanced 1,111-hour subset used in downstream experiments.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 release terms plus YouTube and uploader rights
license.notes: The project requires attribution, non-commercial use, and share-alike derivatives. Those terms do not replace YouTube platform terms, uploader rights, privacy review, or clip-level permissions for the underlying media.

known_limitations: Camera poses and depth are model-generated rather than metric ground truth and can fail under severe distortion, changing focal length, occlusion, or object-dominated scenes.
Dynamic masks derived from motion probabilities can underperform in complex scenes.
The motion-keyword collection and manual screening pipeline favor smooth, reconstructable camera trajectories and may narrow geographic, cultural, subject, and motion diversity.
Source-video availability and legal usability remain dependent on YouTube and uploader rights despite the hosted release.

processing.recipe: Query YouTube with motion-oriented keywords; manually screen long videos; cut 3 to 15 second scenes; normalize to 1280x720 H.265; apply hierarchical quality and motion filtering; reconstruct camera motion and depth; generate dynamic masks, structured captions, and serialized motion instructions; then balance SpatialVID-HQ by motion and scene category.
processing.notes: Use the official downloader and per-clip annotation folders; retain the source video ID, pose convention, depth representation, dynamic mask, caption fields, and license acceptance record.

datasets.name: TalkVid
datasets.description: A multilingual high-definition talking-video research corpus described at 1,244.33 hours, with a richly annotated 160-hour core and a stratified benchmark; the current public Hugging Face artifact exposes only 500 test rows.

access.notes: The current repository contains a 500-row test split of about 2.02 GB; it is not the complete 1,244.33-hour corpus described by the paper and project page.

scale.notes: This card reports the currently observable public artifact; the paper headline is 1,244.33 hours from 7,729 speakers, and TalkVid-Core is 160 hours with 180,860 structured annotations.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-4.0 release terms layered on original YouTube rights
license.notes: The public card uses CC BY-NC 4.0, while source videos remain subject to uploader and platform rights; the release is unsuitable for commercial training without additional clearance.

known_limitations: The public Hugging Face artifact currently exposes only the 500-row benchmark, not the full training corpus claimed by the paper.
DOVER, CoTracker, head-detail filters, Gemini annotations, and human validation can introduce model and reviewer bias.
The project does not publish a complete item-level rights, consent, demographic, or per-language distribution audit.

processing.recipe: Segment more than 6,000 raw hours, filter visual quality and aesthetics with DOVER, bound motion with CoTracker, enforce head-detail criteria, human-validate retained clips, and stratify 500 benchmark clips by age, gender, ethnicity, and language.
processing.notes: Treat the 500-row public test split separately from the unreleased full corpus and 160-hour TalkVid-Core claims.

datasets.name: Seedance 1 Pro Human Preferences
datasets.description: An open set of paired image-to-video outputs and human judgments comparing Seedance 1 Pro with Hailuo-02 and Marey on prompt alignment, visual coherence, and aesthetic preference.

access.notes: Hugging Face hosts the 198-row Parquet table, prompt images, preview assets, and full-resolution model outputs.

scale.notes: The card reports about 6,000 responses from about 2,000 annotators aggregated into 198 paired comparisons.

license.media: Generated-output rights depend on Seedance 1 Pro, Hailuo-02, and Marey service terms
license.notes: Apache-2.0 covers the published repository metadata; users should separately review the terms governing model outputs and prompt images.

known_limitations: The 198 comparison rows are too small to represent the full prompt and motion distribution of the compared services.
The card reports approximate annotator and response counts without demographic or sampling details.
Model versions are fixed historical service snapshots and may not match current production behavior.

processing.notes: Keep individual responses separate from weighted aggregates and group splits by prompt asset to prevent leakage.

datasets.name: SpeakerVid-5M
datasets.description: A 5.2M-clip, 8,743-hour speaker-video metadata corpus covering monadic speaking, listening, and dyadic conversation, with captions, transcripts, poses, face boxes, quality scores, and audio-video synchronization signals.

access.notes: About 58.9 GB of annotations and YouTube identifiers are hosted openly; users reconstruct clips from source videos, and the optional pose archive is not part of the standard hosted media release.

scale.notes: The project reports 5.2M clips and 8,743 hours across pretraining and higher-quality fine-tuning partitions.

license.media: Source-dependent YouTube and rightsholder terms
license.notes: Hosted annotations do not grant rights to the referenced YouTube videos; verify creator permission, privacy, biometric use, and intended training rights separately.

known_limitations: Source-video deletion and regional availability can make metadata records unreconstructable.
Face and pose filtering can bias identity, age, culture, accessibility, camera framing, and speaking-style coverage.
Transcript, caption, pose, and synchronization signals are automatically produced and can contain correlated errors.

processing.notes: Preserve branch, interaction type, source ID, timestamps, transcript, caption, face and pose metadata, DOVER and sync scores, retrieval status, and rights review.

datasets.name: PosterCraft public training corpora
datasets.description: The two public PosterCraft training collections: Text-Render-2M for large-scale text rendering and Poster100K for region-aware high-quality poster tuning.

access.notes: The official organization hosts Text-Render-2M and Poster100K as separate downloadable Hugging Face repositories.

scale.notes: Current repository listings show about 2.15M Text-Render-2M rows and 48.4K Poster100K rows; pin each component revision.

license.media: Poster100K is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0; verify Text-Render-2M terms separately
license.notes: This aggregate card uses the more restrictive known component boundary; review both repository cards and all source and font rights before use.

known_limitations: Combining two repositories can hide different licenses, schemas, and construction pipelines unless component identity is retained.
Poster sources and synthetic fonts may carry additional attribution or reuse constraints.

processing.notes: Preserve the component repository, revision, text regions, OCR fields, captions, and original rights metadata for every sample.

datasets.name: TalkingHeadBench
datasets.organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and Michigan State University
datasets.description: A manually curated audio-video benchmark for detecting modern talking-head deepfakes, with identity-separated splits, six core academic generators, two held-out generators, synchronized audio, and real-video controls.

derived_from.contribution: Driving video and audio signals plus a distinct subset of real videos
derived_from.notes: CelebV-HQ supplies driving signals for synthetic clips and real-video controls; identities are separated from source portraits and evaluation splits.

access.notes: Hugging Face hosts fake and real video splits, extracted audio, source-driving audio, and split manifests.

scale.notes: The paper reports 2,994 curated fake videos and 2,312 real videos; more than 60 percent of initially generated fakes were removed.

license.metadata: MIT on the Hugging Face card; CC-BY-4.0 in the paper supplement
license.media: Component-dependent, including FFHQ CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and CelebV-HQ and FaceForensics++ terms
license.notes: The repository metadata and paper supplement declare different top-level licenses, while source datasets retain their own terms; review every component license before commercial use or redistribution.

known_limitations: The benchmark covers a finite set of generators and identities, so results may not generalize to newer commercial systems.
Audio was corrected in March and April 2026; scores from earlier snapshots are not directly comparable.
The default real-data split differs from the official FaceForensics++ protocol, and the two split variants should not be mixed.

processing.notes: Pin a dataset revision, keep the selected real-data protocol explicit, and preserve identity separation and audio-version provenance in every run.

datasets.name: MVHumanNet++
datasets.description: An annotation-enhanced release of MVHumanNet that adds improved masks and SMPL-X estimates plus normal and depth maps for multi-view human digitization and generative-avatar research.

derived_from.contribution: Original multi-view human captures, identities, outfits, motions, and calibrations
derived_from.notes: MVHumanNet++ retains the MVHumanNet capture corpus and publishes newly processed geometry and segmentation annotations.

access.notes: Users must read the Terms of Use, submit the official form, and use the granted download links.

scale.notes: The underlying full corpus retains MVHumanNet's 645M-frame scope; the current packaged release filters about 7K outfits, uses 16 common camera views, and samples every 25 frames.

license.metadata: MVHumanNet and MVHumanNet++ Terms of Use
license.media: Non-commercial research and educational use only
license.notes: Data use is controlled by the project-specific terms and form; the repository's CC-BY-NC-4.0 code license is not a blanket media license.

known_limitations: Current packaged coverage and sampling are smaller than the headline full-corpus counts.
Normal, depth, segmentation, and SMPL-X outputs are estimated annotations and can contain correlated model errors.
Human biometric and identity data remain sensitive even under non-commercial research terms.

processing.notes: Version the annotation pipeline separately from the underlying captures and keep confidence, camera, outfit, and identity metadata attached.

datasets.name: AudioCaps 2.0
datasets.description: The second AudioCaps release, containing 98,606 human-written caption rows grounded in ten-second AudioSet and YouTube segments, roughly doubling the original audio-caption collection.

derived_from.contribution: Ten-second source segments and AudioSet offsets
derived_from.notes: AudioCaps selects AudioSet-referenced YouTube segments and adds human natural-language captions while retaining the source video ID and temporal offset.

access.notes: Caption CSV files are public, while raw video and audio access requires submitting the maintainer form.

scale.notes: The official v2.0 split counts are 91,256 train, 2,475 validation, and 4,875 test caption rows.

license.metadata: Academic use only; no standalone SPDX dataset license stated
license.media: AudioSet and YouTube source terms; raw media supplied by request
license.notes: The official repository permits the code and dataset for academic purposes only; its MIT repository license must not be treated as a media license.

known_limitations: The 98,606 count is caption rows and is not documented as a unique-clip count.
AudioCaps 2.0 is a 2025 data update not evaluated in the original 2019 paper.
YouTube availability changes over time, so a later fetch can contain fewer usable clips.

processing.notes: Preserve YouTube ID, start offset, split, caption row ID, fetch time, and media hash.

datasets.name: VideoUFO
datasets.organization: ReLER Lab, University of Technology Sydney
datasets.description: A user-focused text-to-video corpus with more than 1.09 million Creative Commons video clips, short and detailed captions, topic labels, temporal boundaries, middle frames, and six VBench-derived quality signals.

access.notes: Hugging Face hosts the metadata and middle-frame dataset plus 200 compressed video archives; the official card estimates the full video download at approximately 800 GB.

scale.notes: The hosted Full split reports 1,091,712 examples spanning 1,291 topics.

license.media: CC-BY-4.0
license.notes: The official card states that released videos are CC BY 4.0; downstream copies and derivatives must preserve attribution and license notices.

known_limitations: Topic selection is derived from VidProM prompts and may inherit the preferences and geographic skew of that user population.
Captions and quality scores are model-generated signals rather than exhaustive human annotations.
The 800 GB archive footprint makes full-corpus validation and local deduplication expensive.

processing.notes: Preserve topic, time-boundary, caption, quality-score, and source-ID fields; verify archive checksums and split by source video to reduce leakage.

datasets.name: TextAtlas5M
datasets.description: A 5.4-million-record, 1.2 TB collection of synthetic and real dense-text images with prompts across documents, slides, covers, scenes, and styled rendering subsets.

access.notes: All ten subsets are hosted on Hugging Face and can be loaded individually with the datasets library.

scale.notes: The current hosted repository reports 5,398,826 rows and about 1.2 TB.

license.metadata: No single license declared in the current dataset card
license.media: Mixed synthetic and source-derived media
license.notes: Review subset construction, font licenses, document and scene sources, and the current repository terms before commercial or redistributed use.

known_limitations: Synthetic typography may not match natural layout and capture artifacts.
License and source-rights information is not uniform across the ten subsets.

processing.notes: Keep subset names and text/layout attributes separate so synthetic, document-derived, and natural-scene records can be audited independently.

datasets.name: JamendoMaxCaps
datasets.description: A large music-caption corpus built from freely licensed Jamendo tracks, with generated natural-language descriptions and imputed metadata designed for text-to-music training and retrieval.

access.notes: The current Hugging Face release exposes 362,298 records and about 1.66 TB of stored audio and metadata without an account gate.

scale.notes: The paper describes more than 200K freely licensed instrumental tracks; the current hosted revision exposes 362,298 dataset rows, so track and row units should remain distinct.

license.media: Jamendo track-specific Creative Commons licenses plus CC-BY-SA-3.0 dataset terms
license.notes: Individual Jamendo tracks can carry different Creative Commons conditions; filter and attribute per track before commercial training or redistribution.

known_limitations: Generated captions and retrieved metadata can contain hallucinations or overgeneralized genre and mood labels.
Instrumental and Creative-Commons availability constraints make the distribution unlike mainstream commercial music catalogs.
Hosted row count is not necessarily the number of unique tracks described in the paper.

processing.notes: Preserve track ID, audio, generated caption, original and imputed metadata, exact per-track license, attribution, and dataset revision.

datasets.name: Señorita-2M
datasets.organization: CUHK, PolyU, Tsinghua University, IntelliFusion, HKU, and UESTC
datasets.description: An instruction-based video-editing corpus built from roughly 389,000 Pexels source videos and six specialist editing or vision pipelines, yielding about 1.95 million released source-target-instruction examples across local, global, conditional, grounding, inpainting, and outpainting tasks.

access.notes: Hugging Face hosts approximately 1.6 TB of WebDataset archives and task-level JSON metadata without a login gate.

scale.notes: Hugging Face estimates 1,950,021 rows; the paper rounds this to 2M edited pairs produced from 388,909 Pexels source videos.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-2.0 dataset terms plus Pexels contributor and platform terms
license.notes: The Hugging Face card applies CC-BY-NC-2.0, but the source media came from Pexels. Pexels' current terms prohibit using its API to build datasets or train ML systems without explicit permission, so the original collection authorization and per-asset rights require separate review.

known_limitations: Most target videos are synthetic edits and can inherit artifacts, failure modes, or biases from the six specialist pipelines and language models.
The public row estimate, paper-level 2M count, and task archive composition use different counting surfaces and should not be treated as exact equivalents.
Pexels source provenance and the permission basis for the original authenticated API collection are not enumerated per sample on the dataset card.
The corpus focuses on short, mostly visual edits and does not cover audio editing, localization, long-form continuity, or the full professional editing distribution.

processing.recipe: Crawl high-resolution Pexels videos through authenticated APIs; caption and detect objects; create local, global, conditional, grounding, inpainting, and outpainting pairs with specialist models; generate instructions; then filter on visual quality, instruction alignment, and source-target similarity.
processing.notes: Preserve the task archive, source-target orientation, instruction, source identifier, and model-generated mask or condition; pin the Hugging Face revision before sharding.

datasets.name: OpenHumanVid
datasets.description: A large human-centric video corpus with detailed captions, skeleton sequences, speech audio, and quality metadata, distributed through an application process for training general human-video generators.

access.notes: Applicants submit the official form and wait for manual review before receiving the current downloadable release; access is not suitable for unattended CI retrieval.

scale.notes: The current project and repository advertise 13.2M samples, 16.7K hours, and about 6.05 TB. The paper describes a larger 52.3M-sample, 70.6K-hour corpus, so consumers must pin the specific release rather than combining these figures.

license.media: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 release terms plus source-specific rights
license.notes: The repository license is non-commercial and no-derivatives; the media originates from publicly available datasets, whose source-specific terms and rights remain applicable.

known_limitations: Current downloadable scale differs materially from the larger corpus described in the paper.
Speech audio is provided where detected but is not guaranteed to be synchronized or suitable for lip-sync supervision without additional filtering.
Manual access review, non-commercial terms, and source-specific rights restrict automated redistribution and production use.
Human, motion, caption, and quality filters can bias coverage across identities, activities, cultures, camera styles, and low-resource languages.

processing.recipe: Decode and crop source media, split it into clips, filter luminance, blur, aesthetics, motion, and technical quality, extract skeleton and speech signals, and produce detailed captions with multiple vision-language teachers and voting-based refinement.
processing.notes: Record the granted release version and preserve source identifiers; apply a separate synchronization stage before using the speech track for audio-driven avatar training.

datasets.name: Koala-36M
datasets.description: A large video-text corpus built with transition-aware temporal splitting, long structured captions, and a learned video-training-suitability score for text-to-video pretraining and condition-aware data selection.

access.notes: The hosted release contains clip URLs, timestamps, captions, and quality scores rather than redistributable source video files.

scale.notes: Hugging Face estimates 35,961,606 rows; the paper and project round the collection to 36M clips.

license.media: Source-dependent YouTube terms and uploader rights
license.notes: The official dataset card does not state a dataset-specific license; URL metadata does not grant rights to download, train on, or redistribute source videos.

known_limitations: The release is a URL and metadata index, so availability can change when source videos are removed or restricted.
Very long model-generated captions can contain hallucinations or emphasize details that are weakly visible in the clip.
The learned suitability score encodes annotator and model preferences and can narrow cultural, stylistic, and motion diversity.

processing.notes: Preserve the source URL and timestamps, revalidate media rights, and pin the metadata revision before resolving any video.

datasets.name: FineVideo
datasets.description: A collection of Creative Commons YouTube videos with rich descriptions, scene-level structure, transcripts, and question-answer annotations.

access.notes: Users must accept dataset terms before accessing the repository.

scale.notes: The maintainers report over 43K videos spanning about 3.4K hours.

license.media: Per-video Creative Commons terms
license.notes: Users must preserve attribution and provenance, follow current usable versions and removals, and include the dataset terms when sharing access.

known_limitations: Long-form videos are not equivalent to generation-ready short clips.
The usable version can change when validated removal requests are processed.

processing.notes: Use scene annotations to derive clips and retain attribution per source video.

datasets.name: Re-LAION-5B
datasets.description: A safety-revised release of LAION-5B metadata intended to remove known harmful links while preserving a reproducible web-scale image-text index.

access.notes: LAION distributes metadata rather than the underlying image files.

scale.notes: Derived from the 5.85B-pair LAION-5B index after safety revisions.

license.media: Source-dependent and not distributed by LAION
license.notes: Metadata licensing does not grant copyright or other rights to images resolved from third-party URLs. Apply takedowns and current safety lists.

known_limitations: Web metadata can be noisy, biased, unsafe, or stale.
The reconstructed media corpus changes as source URLs disappear.

processing.notes: Re-check hashes, safety signals, access results, and rights at ingestion time.

datasets.name: Emilia
datasets.description: A large multilingual in-the-wild speech dataset produced with the Emilia-Pipe preprocessing system, covering roughly 101,000 hours across English, Chinese, Japanese, French, German, and Korean.

access.notes: Hosted WebDataset archives and preprocessing code are available from the official Amphion repository; review the dataset card before downloading at scale.

scale.notes: The official release announcement reports 101K hours; shard and utterance counts can change with repository revisions.

license.metadata: CC-BY-NC-4.0 as declared in the official dataset card metadata
license.media: Review source-media rights and the official dataset terms for each use
license.notes: The repository UI and card history have shown inconsistent CC-BY and CC-BY-NC labels; this card uses the stricter CC-BY-NC-4.0 declaration and requires a fresh license review before redistribution.

known_limitations: Automated source discovery, diarization, recognition, and filtering can retain transcription and speaker-boundary errors.
In-the-wild speech can contain personal, copyrighted, biased, or sensitive content.
License metadata has been inconsistent across repository renderings and must be rechecked for downstream releases.

processing.notes: Preserve language, source and shard provenance, validate transcripts and speaker boundaries, run privacy and rights screening, and document excluded samples.

datasets.name: Flickr 5B metadata
datasets.description: A very large Flickr metadata collection whose rows provide image URLs at multiple resolutions plus available license, geolocation, date, description, and machine-tag fields; it does not redistribute a canonical media archive.

access.notes: The Hugging Face repository distributes sharded URL metadata; an account or authentication may be required, and each source image can disappear independently.

scale.notes: The current dataset description says approximately 5B Flickr images; earlier snapshots and mirrors reported smaller row counts.

license.media: Rights and Creative Commons terms vary by the original Flickr item
license.notes: ODC-By applies to the metadata database, not automatically to every linked image; users must preserve item-level licenses and verify current source rights.

known_limitations: URL survival, rate limits, and access permissions change over time.
Web descriptions and tags are noisy and are not guaranteed to describe visible content.
The repository-scale count has changed across published snapshots and should be treated as approximate.

processing.notes: Stream metadata shards, retain the original row and item license, fetch only permitted media, record fetch time and result, hash payloads, and deduplicate before use.

datasets.name: OpenVid-1M
datasets.description: A curated collection of one million high-quality video clips with expressive captions, including a large high-definition subset for video generation.

access.notes: Videos, CSV metadata, and split archives are hosted on Hugging Face.

scale.notes: The project reports about 1M clips, including 433K clips at 1080p.

license.media: Source-dependent with research and non-commercial restrictions stated
license.notes: The dataset card asks users to follow licenses of upstream video datasets and states a research and non-commercial intent despite the CC-BY label.

known_limitations: Upstream datasets have different or unknown media terms.
Curated aesthetic distributions may narrow content diversity.

processing.notes: Validate archives, normalize codecs, and preserve upstream dataset provenance.

datasets.name: AutoReCap-XL
datasets.description: A large automatically recaptioned audio-text corpus derived from YouTube video segments, with a 47M-pair released XL set and progressively filtered MQ, MQ-L, and HQ subsets based on CLAP alignment and duration.

access.notes: About 17.4 GB of JSON metadata is hosted on Hugging Face; the official scripts reconstruct audio from referenced source videos rather than distributing raw media.

scale.notes: The released variants contain 47M XL, 20.7M MQ, 14.7M MQ-L, and 10.7M HQ pairs; the original paper describes a 57M-candidate collection before the final release filtering.

license.media: Source-dependent YouTube and rightsholder terms
license.notes: The project limits the release to non-commercial research; raw audio is reconstructed from YouTube and remains subject to source rights and platform terms.

known_limitations: Automatic speech and music keyword removal can suppress useful mixed or ambiguous sound events.
Generated captions and CLAP thresholds can reinforce the teacher model's vocabulary and alignment biases.
Source videos can disappear or change, and the released metadata does not convey media rights.

processing.notes: Preserve source ID, timestamps, original transcript signal, generated caption, CLAP score, subset membership, retrieval date, and rights decision.

datasets.name: ChronoMagic-Pro
datasets.description: A 460K-example time-lapse video-text corpus for learning physical processes and long-range metamorphic motion, with a 150K-example high-quality ProH subset selected for visual quality and caption alignment.

access.notes: Roughly 2.06 TB of videos and metadata are hosted on Hugging Face without a gate.

scale.notes: The official project reports 460K time-lapse videos and a 150K high-quality ChronoMagic-ProH subset.

license.media: CC-BY-4.0 dataset label plus source-video terms
license.notes: The hosted card is tagged CC-BY-4.0, but original video rights and any source-platform conditions should be checked before commercial training or redistribution.

known_limitations: Time-lapse capture and web sourcing bias the corpus toward visible processes and popular subjects.
Automated captioning and quality scoring can miss subtle process direction, duration, or causal details.
The headline corpus and ProH subset should not be combined as independent samples.

processing.notes: Preserve full versus ProH membership, time-lapse category, original duration and frame rate, caption, quality scores, and source identifier.

datasets.name: Infinity-Instruct
datasets.description: A versioned, multilingual family of millions of selected and evolved instruction-response records with task labels and reward scores for scalable supervised and preference tuning.

access.notes: Multiple versions and configurations are hosted as Parquet; consumers should pin the exact configuration and revision used.

scale.notes: The project targets a 10M family and exposes several 3M, 7M, core, generated, and chat configurations rather than one immutable split.

license.media: Text records subject to component-source and share-alike terms
license.notes: The hosted dataset is marked CC BY-SA 4.0, while downstream users must retain attribution, share-alike obligations, and component provenance.

known_limitations: Version names cover materially different source, selected, evolved, and preference subsets.
Model-generated instructions and reward labels can transmit evaluator and teacher-model bias.

processing.notes: Pin configuration and revision, retain source and reward metadata, and deduplicate against downstream evaluation and preference sets.

datasets.name: MVHumanNet
datasets.description: A large multi-view daily-dressing human capture corpus with identities, outfits, motion sequences, calibrated imagery, parametric bodies, and text descriptions for human rendering, reconstruction, and avatar generation.

access.notes: Users accept the project terms, submit a form, and receive expiring download links for the released parts.

scale.notes: The full project scope is 645M frames, 60K motion sequences, 9K outfits, and 4.5K identities; the repository says the public Part 1 plus Part 2 release covers about 4K identities and 8K outfits.

license.media: Non-commercial research and educational use only
license.notes: The data follows the project-specific Terms of Use; the repository's CC-BY-NC-4.0 license is stated for code and must not be assumed to replace the data agreement.

known_limitations: Full-scale headline counts differ from the currently documented public release coverage.
The capture setup and selected outfits, identities, motions, and camera views may bias downstream avatars toward the collection protocol.
Consent, identity, biometric, and clothing-rights constraints require review before any derived model is deployed.

processing.notes: Preserve outfit, identity, sequence, camera, calibration, body-model, and terms-of-use lineage through every derived view or mesh.

datasets.name: Panda-70M
datasets.description: A large video-caption corpus produced by splitting source videos into semantically consistent clips and captioning them with multiple teachers.

access.notes: CSV metadata and download tooling are provided for source videos.

scale.notes: Statistics refer to the full training split reported by the project.

license.media: Source-dependent
license.notes: The maintainers require users to follow the related license of publicly sourced video samples; availability is primarily metadata plus tooling.

known_limitations: Download success and the resulting corpus vary with source availability.
Machine captions and scores can propagate teacher-model biases.

processing.notes: Retain source video IDs and clip timestamps through download and sharding.

datasets.name: CommonCatalog
datasets.description: A family of filtered YFCC100M image subsets with item-level Creative Commons provenance and BLIP-2 synthetic captions, released in commercial and non-commercial license partitions for reproducible text-to-image training.

derived_from.contribution: Flickr identifiers, source metadata, and Creative Commons licensed media pool
derived_from.notes: CommonCatalog re-resolves YFCC100M images, excludes non-derivative licenses, filters the media, and adds BLIP-2 captions.

access.notes: Six Hugging Face repositories partition the corpus by CC-BY, SA, NC, and combined license variants.

scale.notes: The paper reports 67,015,331 images in CommonCatalog-NC, including a 26,232,417-image commercial-use subset; hosted per-license shard counts sum to the same family-level scope.

license.media: Item-level CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, and non-commercial variants; non-derivative items excluded
license.notes: Only the C subset is designed for commercial use; every use must preserve attribution and follow the exact item's Creative Commons variant.

known_limitations: BLIP-2 captions are synthetic, mostly English, and can omit identity, context, or culturally specific details.
The source is decade-old Flickr data with geographic, demographic, and photographic-style skews.
Corpus-level labels do not remove the need for item-level attribution, privacy, and takedown handling.

processing.notes: Keep license partitions separate, retain attribution fields, and never mix the NC shards into a commercial training run.

datasets.name: Pick-a-Pic v2
datasets.organization: Tel Aviv University and Meta AI
datasets.description: An open collection of real user choices between pairs of text-to-image model outputs, with prompts and preference labels for alignment research.

access.notes: The canonical Hugging Face repository currently requires authenticated access.

scale.notes: The v2 release is described as containing more than one million examples.

license.media: Model-output and source-term dependent
license.notes: Confirm the current dataset card and the terms of image-generating models; a dataset license may not resolve every right in generated outputs.

known_limitations: Online user preferences are self-selected and not demographically representative.
Repeated prompts, users, and model versions can create leakage or dependence.

processing.notes: Split by prompt and user provenance where possible to reduce evaluation leakage.

datasets.name: FreeMan
datasets.description: A real-world multi-view human-motion dataset captured with eight synchronized smartphones, pairing RGB video with cameras, 2D and 3D keypoints, SMPL parameters, and bounding boxes for human sensing and digital-human research.

access.notes: Access requires a signed usage agreement, an application form, and approval on Hugging Face or OpenXLab.

scale.notes: The project reports 11.3M frames from 8,000 sequences, 40 subjects, 10 scenario types, and eight movable camera views.

license.media: Research-only participant data under the signed FreeMan agreement
license.notes: Official pages differ between CC-BY-NC-4.0 and CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 wording; the signed agreement and current download terms control use.

known_limitations: The dataset contains only 40 consenting subjects and cannot represent the full range of identities, bodies, clothing, or mobility.
Real-world capture improves scene diversity but introduces occlusion, lighting, calibration, and pose-estimation noise.
Human biometric and motion data require privacy review even when the original collection used consent and anonymization procedures.

processing.notes: Keep sequence, subject, camera, calibration, consent, and usage-agreement metadata attached to every derived artifact.

datasets.name: InternVid
datasets.description: A web-scale video-text corpus built from millions of source videos and segmented into captioned clips for multimodal understanding and generation.

access.notes: Public releases include metadata and filtered subsets such as InternVid-10M-FLT.

scale.notes: Paper-level full-corpus statistics; accessible subsets may be much smaller.

license.media: Source-dependent
license.notes: The Apache-2.0 repository license covers code, not necessarily third-party web videos. Review the dataset card and each intended media use.

known_limitations: Full paper scale and currently downloadable subsets are not equivalent.
Web video availability, safety, and rights can change over time.

processing.notes: Record subset name and version before comparing results or publishing counts.

datasets.name: Objaverse-XL
datasets.description: A web-scale collection of more than ten million deduplicated 3D objects from multiple public sources, designed to support 3D foundation models and large multiview-rendering pipelines.

access.notes: Official tooling resolves source assets; some subsets, notably Polycam, require separate access.

scale.notes: The project reports over 10 million 3D objects rather than a fixed frozen count.

license.media: Per-object source license
license.notes: Dataset metadata is ODC-By-1.0, while each object retains its source license; the Polycam contribution is explicitly non-commercial and separately gated.

known_limitations: Asset formats, geometry quality, topology, textures, and metadata vary substantially by source.
Source objects may disappear or change after a metadata snapshot is published.
